sourceEnglish: Watch: Draw the Land You Already Have
currentTarget: Sedzani: Draw the Land You Already Have
previousCandidate: Sedzani: Olani land ine ya no vha yaṋu
proposedTarget: Sedzani: Olani land ine na no vha nayo
backtranslation: Watch: Draw the land you already have.

analysis.already: no is a defensible already/completed-state aspect here. Primary DBE text attests ro no vha nayo in a have-already construction, not merely now.
analysis.have: vha nayo expresses having/being with it; removing yaṋu avoids the previous is-yours predicate. No legal-title or acquisition claim is added.
analysis.subject: na is plausible second-person plural/honorific relative subject corresponding to instructional ni; primary DBE relative clauses attest ine na ... nayo.
analysis.concord: The retained English land is treated in the same class9-compatible ine/nayo agreement as the earlier have proposal. The primary examples support the construction pieces, not a proof that the full new borrowed-noun heading is fluent.
analysis.prefix: Existing Sedzani: is preserved; Olani translates Draw. No scope, times, prescriptions or extra ownership qualification.

primaryEvidence.title: DBE Tshivenda HL P2 February–March2015 memorandum
primaryEvidence.exactExcerpt: mbofholowo ya u amba ro no vha nayo kha ndayotewa.
primaryEvidence.boundedInference: We already have the freedom of speech in the constitution: ro no vha nayo supports already+have, with another person concord.
primaryEvidence.access: Primary PDF textual extract read; screenshot request timed out and is not claimed visually verified.

primaryEvidence.title: DBE Mind the Gap Nandi ndi Shenga study guide
primaryEvidence.exactExcerpt: Khuḓano ine na ḓo ṱangana nayo i simuwa hone.
primaryEvidence.boundedInference: Relative ine na ... nayo addresses the reader; illustrates relative subject/object concord but not the already aspect itself.
primaryEvidence.access: Primary indexed PDF textual extract read; legacy encoded diacritics normalized for this excerpt.

inferenceLimits: Exact full phrase ine na no vha nayo was not located in the bounded primary search.
Acceptance is a semantic plausibility judgment combining attested already-have and relative-address constructions; not fluent concord approval.
The new heading retains land English but no longer retains ordinary already English.
No required new fluent-speaker prepublication gate is asserted; root retains adoption decision.
